Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including its electronic headquarters at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. Customs and excise administration is also conducted through the AEAT, subject to applicable European Union customs and excise systems.

E-government filing portal

A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a provisional Spanish Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) during incorporation and a definitive NIF after registration of the deed and corporate particulars with the Commercial Registry. The company files Modelo 036 with the AEAT, submits the incorporation deed, Commercial Registry documentation, constitutional documents, registered office evidence, identification of directors and beneficial owners, and powers of attorney where applicable. The NIF is used as the Spanish VAT identification number, generally displayed internationally with the prefix ES. Registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and activation of the VIES status are requested through Modelo 036 before intra-Community acquisitions, supplies, or services requiring VAT identification. A foreign entity without a Spanish permanent establishment may request a Spanish NIF through Modelo 036 and must provide certified corporate documents, proof of legal existence, identification of representatives, and, where required, a Spanish tax representative. Non-EU businesses may be required to appoint a Spanish VAT representative, subject to statutory exceptions and applicable mutual-assistance arrangements. Customs activities additionally require an Economic Operators Registration and Identification (EORI) number, normally obtained through the AEAT customs system.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation. Non-resident shareholders are taxed separately on dividends, capital gains, or other Spanish-source income, subject to domestic law, European Union rules, and applicable tax treaties. VAT and excise obligations are separate from Corporate Income Tax status. Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation. A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is a separate taxpayer for Spanish Corporate Income Tax and is generally subject to tax on worldwide income if it is tax resident in Spain. Spanish tax residence normally arises from incorporation under Spanish law, registered office in Spain, or effective management in Spain. Non-resident shareholders are taxed separately on dividends, capital gains, or other Spanish-source income, subject to domestic law, European Union rules, and applicable tax treaties. VAT and excise obligations are separate from Corporate Income Tax status. Craft beer distribution may also trigger Spanish beer excise duty, packaging obligations, and warehouse or movement-control requirements.

Available election forms

Spain has no general United States-style check-the-box election for an SL. Available statutory regimes and elections may include Corporate Income Tax consolidation for qualifying corporate groups, the special regime for entities holding foreign securities (ETVE) where statutory conditions are satisfied, the Spanish VAT group regime, the cash-accounting VAT regime (Régimen Especial del Criterio de Caja) where eligibility requirements are met, and voluntary inclusion in the Immediate Supply of Information system (SII). Spanish transparent-entity treatment applies only to legally qualifying vehicles and is not an elective classification for an ordinary SL. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules implementing the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive apply mandatorily; there is no elective hybrid-mismatch classification. Participation in the EU One Stop Shop may be available for qualifying intra-EU distance sales and electronically supplied or other covered services, but it does not replace domestic registration where the Spanish company makes domestic taxable supplies.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

EUR 0 for general Spanish VAT registration purposes. Spain has no general turnover threshold below which a business making taxable supplies may remain outside VAT registration. A taxable person must register in the census of entrepreneurs, professionals, and withholders before commencing activities or making relevant taxable transactions. Separate EU thresholds and reporting rules may apply to intra-Community distance sales and special regimes, but they do not create a general domestic Spanish VAT registration threshold.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods dispatched or transported from Spain to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT under Spanish VAT law, provided the statutory exporter, transport, customs, and documentary conditions are satisfied. The supplier or an acting intermediary must be able to demonstrate that the goods physically left the EU customs territory and that the supply is correctly linked to the export declaration and commercial invoice. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for exemption with the right to deduct where the customer is VAT-identified in another EU Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, the supplier has valid evidence of transport, and the transaction is correctly reported, including the recapitulative statement where required. Services supplied to a business customer established outside Spain may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule rather than technically zero-rated; evidence of customer business status and establishment outside Spain is required. Beer exports may also require compliance with excise-duty procedures, including EMCS documentation where goods move under duty suspension, authorized warehousekeeper or registered consignor requirements, and proof of exit.

  • Customs Export Declaration containing the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and export procedure data
  • Electronic confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory or equivalent customs exit certification
  • Commercial invoice identifying the Spanish supplier, purchaser, goods, quantities, values, VAT treatment, and delivery terms
  • Packing list and transport documentation, including Bill of Lading, sea waybill, air waybill, CMR, or equivalent evidence
  • Proof linking the goods to the export declaration, including container, consignment, batch, keg, or shipment references where relevant
  • Import or customs documentation from the destination country where reasonably obtainable
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or bank evidence of payment where required by the business's internal controls, financing arrangements, or foreign-exchange compliance procedures; Spain does not generally require a universal inward-remittance certificate as a condition for VAT export exemption
  • For excise goods, applicable EMCS administrative reference code, e-AD or simplified accompanying document, tax-warehouse records, and proof of discharge or export

Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for every invoice. Taxable persons subject to SII must electronically transmit specified VAT ledger information to the AEAT, generally within four calendar days, excluding Sundays and national holidays, subject to special rules for invoices issued by the recipient and transport-related circumstances. SII is mandatory principally for businesses exceeding the statutory large-business turnover threshold, VAT groups, entities registered in REDEME, and entities electing into SII. Royal Decree 1007/2023 requires compliant billing and accounting software to preserve integrity, traceability, immutability, sequentiality, event logging, and anti-tampering controls, with QR and hash requirements and a VERI*FACTU transmission option; implementation dates and technical specifications must be verified against the latest implementing amendments. Law 18/2022 establishes a phased B2B electronic-invoicing framework, dependent on implementing regulations and the applicable turnover-based timetable. Public-sector invoicing may require FACe or another authorized platform. Invoices must contain mandatory Spanish and EU VAT particulars, including supplier and customer identification, VAT number where applicable, taxable base, rate, VAT amount, invoice number, date, and applicable exemption or reverse-charge wording.

Spain has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline requiring export proceeds to be brought into Spain within 180 days. Export proceeds remain subject to ordinary banking, anti-money-laundering, accounting, transfer-pricing, and debt-collection controls. If an export exemption or intra-Community exemption is unsupported, the AEAT may reassess output VAT, deny or claw back input-VAT deductions or refunds, charge late-payment interest, and impose tax penalties under the General Tax Law. Penalties for serious or very serious VAT infringements can commonly range from 50% to 150% of the improperly unpaid or refunded tax, depending on the infringement, concealment, repeated conduct, and aggravating factors. False, manipulated, or incomplete customs evidence may result in customs debt, recovery of duties and taxes, customs sanctions, loss of simplified procedures or authorizations, and excise-duty liability. Incorrect invoicing, failure to maintain records, or failure to submit electronic VAT information may generate separate fixed or proportional penalties. Deliberate tax fraud may also create criminal exposure where statutory thresholds and elements are met. The company should retain export, transport, customs, excise, customer, payment, and inventory evidence for the applicable Spanish limitation period, generally four years for tax assessment purposes, subject to suspension, interruption, special record-retention rules, and longer periods applicable to certain assets or criminal matters.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is a euro-area Member State; the euro is fully convertible. Capital movements and current payments are unrestricted under Articles 63-65 TFEU. No prior exchange-control authorization or foreign-exchange license is required for inbound share-capital contributions, trade settlements, or profit remittances by a Sociedad de Limitada. The only binding duties are statistical declarations to Banco de España for cross-border flows exceeding EUR 50,000 (or equivalent) and compliance with tax withholding rules. Profit repatriation is free once financial statements are approved and corporate tax filings are filed; non-resident dividends are subject to statutory withholding at 19% but may be reduced under an applicable tax treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where beneficial-ownership conditions are satisfied.

Export proceeds surrender rules

There is no statutory export proceeds surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio. Spanish exporters may collect proceeds in EUR or in freely convertible foreign currency and may retain foreign-currency balances in authorized banks. Export receipts must be supported by customs documentation (including the Single Administrative Document/DUA), commercial contracts, and transport bills. Cross-border receipts above EUR 50,000 must be reported in the Banco de España balance-of-payments statistical declarations. No deadline applies for repatriation, conversion, or surrender of export proceeds.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) and, for foreign trade reporting and investment statistics, the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio of the Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium. EEA-licensed digital payment institutions passported into Spain under PSD2 are viable for operational FX, SEPA collection, and cross-border payment routing. Non-EEA offshore EMIs are not legally able to provide payment accounts without a Spanish/EU license or passport. The SL should retain at least one Tier-1 Spanish credit institution with a Spanish IBAN for tax payments, customs duties, and documentary trade; a fintech EMI can serve as a secondary treasury rail but is not suitable for statutory capital escrow or large documentary credit settlements.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Newly incorporated SL with a non-resident beneficial owner and no operating history

Root cause: Newly incorporated SL with a non-resident beneficial owner and no operating history

Defense evidence: Notarized deed of incorporation, NIF certificate, corporate by-laws, passport and tax-residence certificate for every director/ultimate beneficial owner, source-of-funds bank statements for subscribed capital, a signed operations plan, projected trade flows, and financial references from the shareholder's primary bank.
Regulated alcoholic-beverage wholesale activity (craft beer distribution)

Root cause: Regulated alcoholic-beverage wholesale activity (craft beer distribution)

Defense evidence: Valid commercial license for alcoholic-beverage distribution, municipal activity license, Agencia Tributaria excise-duty registration, Ministry of Agriculture/Food Safety registration, EORI number, product specification sheets, labeling compliance, warehouse lease, and import/export supply contracts.
Large inbound capital contribution from an overseas shareholder

Root cause: Large inbound capital contribution from an overseas shareholder

Defense evidence: Shareholder resolution approving the capital contribution, notarized board minutes, current deeds and registry filings, audited or certified financial statements of the transferring shareholder, foreign bank reference letter, declaration of beneficial ownership, and a formal source-of-wealth statement supported by bank records.
High-volume, low-margin wholesale transaction pattern

Root cause: High-volume, low-margin wholesale transaction pattern

Defense evidence: Purchase orders, commercial invoices, transport documents (CMR, bill of lading), customs declarations, warehouse inventory records, distribution agreements, and a coherent margin analysis demonstrating legitimate trade economics rather than trade-based money laundering.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Non-resident shareholders transmit funds by SWIFT MT103 for non-EU wire transfers or SEPA Credit Transfer for EU transfers, referencing 'Capital contribution / subscription of participaciones sociales' and providing the Spanish SL's IBAN at a Tier-1 domestic bank. Funds are received into a segregated capital-escrow account and may not be used operationally until the capital increase is formalized before a notary and registered. The receiving bank requires the deed, NIF/NIE documents, tax-residence certificates, source-of-funds evidence, and the applicable balance-of-payments statistical concept code for direct investment. No exchange-control authorization is required, but the inward transfer must be reported to Banco de España through the bank when the amount exceeds EUR 50,000.Trade settlements are executed through SWIFT MT103 for international supplier wires, SEPA Direct Debit and SEPA Credit Transfer for EU counterparties, and local Direct Debit for Spanish brewery collections. For high-value or letter-of-credit confirmed purchases from US and Latin American suppliers, the SL should use a documentary commercial LC with a confirming bank, presenting the commercial invoice, bill of lading, insurance certificate, and sanitary/labeling export documentation. Treasury bank accounts should be segregated by function to evidence trade purpose and to prevent mixing of operational payroll, shareholder loans, and intercompany fees.Outright foreign-exchange forwards (deliverable)Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-deliverable or emerging-market currenciesFX swapsCross-currency interest-rate swapsEuropean-style currency options (buy/sell puts and calls)

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium. EEA-licensed digital payment institutions passported into Spain under PSD2 are viable for operational FX, SEPA collection, and cross-border payment routing. Non-EEA offshore EMIs are not legally able to provide payment accounts without a Spanish/EU license or passport. The SL should retain at least one Tier-1 Spanish credit institution with a Spanish IBAN for tax payments, customs duties, and documentary trade; a fintech EMI can serve as a secondary treasury rail but is not suitable for statutory capital escrow or large documentary credit settlements.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days following the six months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., for a 31 December year-end, filing window is 1–25 July).

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 00001 (Identificación) Tax identification number (NIF), legal form, registered address, and dominant activity code (CNAE). Enter the permanent establishment's NIF; if filing as a non-resident without a PE, use Modelo 025 instead. Use Spanish tax identification rules for foreign entities (NIF-E for non-resident without establishment). Late filing penalty: 5% of the amount due if filed within 3 months of the deadline; 10% if between 3–6 months; 15% if between 6–12 months; 20% if after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75%/year). For no amount due, a flat fine of €200. Understatement penalties range from 50% to 150% of the omitted amount under art. 191 LGT.
Box 00002 (Devengo y período impositivo) Tax period start and end dates, indicating whether the period is shorter than 12 months due to incorporation or cessation. Report the same tax period as the local branch's audited financial statements; ensure alignment with the home country fiscal year for treaty consistency. Late filing penalty: 5% of the amount due if filed within 3 months of the deadline; 10% if between 3–6 months; 15% if between 6–12 months; 20% if after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75%/year). For no amount due, a flat fine of €200. Understatement penalties range from 50% to 150% of the omitted amount under art. 191 LGT.
Box 00127 (Resultado contable) Net accounting profit before tax according to Spanish GAAP, after depreciation, provisions, and inventory adjustments. For a PE, reflect only Spain-sourced commercial activity, applying the separate enterprise principle; ensure cold-chain logistics costs are properly allocated. Late filing penalty: 5% of the amount due if filed within 3 months of the deadline; 10% if between 3–6 months; 15% if between 6–12 months; 20% if after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75%/year). For no amount due, a flat fine of €200. Understatement penalties range from 50% to 150% of the omitted amount under art. 191 LGT.
Boxes 00131–00233 (Ajustes extracontables) Permanent and temporary differences: non-deductible expenses, tax depreciation, amortization of goodwill, and impairment reversals. Reclassify head-office general expenses recharged to the PE under the OECD authorised approach; only real, documented recharges are deductible. Late filing penalty: 5% of the amount due if filed within 3 months of the deadline; 10% if between 3–6 months; 15% if between 6–12 months; 20% if after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75%/year). For no amount due, a flat fine of €200. Understatement penalties range from 50% to 150% of the omitted amount under art. 191 LGT.
Box 00547 (Compensación de bases imponibles negativas) Offset of prior-year tax loss carryforwards against the current taxable base, subject to the 70% limit (€1 million exempt) for large taxpayers. Apply any treaty non-discrimination clauses; BINs generated after 2020 by PEs are subject to the same 70% cap, with no specific PE exception. Late filing penalty: 5% of the amount due if filed within 3 months of the deadline; 10% if between 3–6 months; 15% if between 6–12 months; 20% if after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75%/year). For no amount due, a flat fine of €200. Understatement penalties range from 50% to 150% of the omitted amount under art. 191 LGT.
Box 00581 (Base imponible) Taxable base after accounting result, extra-contractual adjustments, and BIN compensation. Ensure the PE's taxable base excludes non-Spanish source income unless the treaty allocates it to Spain; maintain a functional analysis for allocation. Late filing penalty: 5% of the amount due if filed within 3 months of the deadline; 10% if between 3–6 months; 15% if between 6–12 months; 20% if after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75%/year). For no amount due, a flat fine of €200. Understatement penalties range from 50% to 150% of the omitted amount under art. 191 LGT.
Box 00591 (Tipo de gravamen y cuota íntegra) Application of the 25% general rate or the 15% reduced rate for qualifying new SMEs. A PE is generally taxed at 25%; the 15% rate applies only to resident new SMEs meeting the turnover and capital requirements. Late filing penalty: 5% of the amount due if filed within 3 months of the deadline; 10% if between 3–6 months; 15% if between 6–12 months; 20% if after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75%/year). For no amount due, a flat fine of €200. Understatement penalties range from 50% to 150% of the omitted amount under art. 191 LGT.
Box 00595 (Deducciones y bonificaciones) Double taxation relief, R&D credits, environmental investment credits, and export-related deductions. Apply foreign tax credit for income sourced outside Spain and taxed in the home country if the PE is treated as a separate entity; no credit for taxes paid by the head office on PE income. Late filing penalty: 5% of the amount due if filed within 3 months of the deadline; 10% if between 3–6 months; 15% if between 6–12 months; 20% if after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75%/year). For no amount due, a flat fine of €200. Understatement penalties range from 50% to 150% of the omitted amount under art. 191 LGT.
Box 00615 (Retenciones y pagos fraccionados) Offset of Spanish withholding taxes and quarterly instalment payments already made. Reconcile Spanish withholding certificates (Modelo 193) with the PE's income; non-resident suppliers are subject to 19%/24% WHT, and the PE must correctly gross up payments. Late filing penalty: 5% of the amount due if filed within 3 months of the deadline; 10% if between 3–6 months; 15% if between 6–12 months; 20% if after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75%/year). For no amount due, a flat fine of €200. Understatement penalties range from 50% to 150% of the omitted amount under art. 191 LGT.
Box 00623 (Cuota diferencial / resultante) Final tax due after offsets and credits, or refundable amount. If a refund is due, it is processed automatically through Modelo 200 unless the taxpayer opts for a separate refund request. No additional form is required. Late filing penalty: 5% of the amount due if filed within 3 months of the deadline; 10% if between 3–6 months; 15% if between 6–12 months; 20% if after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75%/year). For no amount due, a flat fine of €200. Understatement penalties range from 50% to 150% of the omitted amount under art. 191 LGT.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Local File and Master File required for related-party transactions exceeding EUR 250,000 in aggregate per year (art. 13 LIS). Additionally, a simplified documentation regime applies to small entities with turnover below €10 million and transactions under €1 million. Modelo 232 informative return is mandatory when aggregate related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not have standalone ESR; however, the general anti-abuse rule (art. 15 LGT), the sham transaction doctrine, and the BEPS substance requirements apply. A Spanish entity (SL) must demonstrate actual personnel, offices, decision-making, and operational activity, particularly for the physical distribution of craft beer (cold-chain logistics, warehousing, delivery). Offshore outsourcing without substance will be challenged under art. 107 LIS and treaty anti-abuse rules.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion (Defraudación Tributaria)

Statutory sanction: Criminal conviction under art. 305 Penal Code if the defrauded amount exceeds €120,000: imprisonment 1–5 years, fines of 2–6 times the defrauded amount, and loss of tax benefits and subsidies. Administrative penalty (arts. 191–192 LGT) of 50%–150% of the understated amount plus interest. False invoices can trigger fines of €1,500 per invoice (up to €300,000).

Director personal liability: Directors as 'responsables subsidiarios' (art. 43 LGT) may be personally liable for 50% of the corporate tax debt if they intentionally tolerated non-payment. In criminal cases, directors can be imprisoned (up to 5 years) and may face travel bans and attachment of personal assets. The corporate veil is pierced for fraud.
Money Laundering (Blanqueo de Capitales)

Statutory sanction: Administrative fines under Law 10/2010 up to €5,000,000, public reprimand, and disqualification of compliance officers. Criminal money laundering (art. 301 Penal Code) carries imprisonment 6 months–6 years and fines. Bank accounts, inventory, and delivery vehicles may be seized.

Director personal liability: Directors who knowingly participate or fail to prevent money laundering are criminally co-responsible; personal assets are subject to confiscation. Travel bans and residency restrictions may be imposed for up to 10 years.
Transfer Pricing and Substance Failure

Statutory sanction: Penalties under art. 18 LIS: €1,000 per missing document, up to €50,000. For Modelo 232, penalty of €10,000 per omitted declaration (minimum €5,000). If adjustments are made, the taxpayer pays tax differential plus interest; TP penalties range from 15%–30% of the increase in taxable income.

Director personal liability: Directors signing the Modelo 200 while knowingly using unjustified TP reports are subject to administrative penalties. If the adjustment understatement exceeds €120,000, criminal tax evasion charges may be brought, exposing directors to imprisonment up to 5 years.
Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement

Statutory sanction: Under art. 107 LIS, the AEAT recharacterizes the activity and attributes it to the effective management location; the entity loses tax treaty benefits and is taxed at 25% on full revenue without deductions for intercompany costs. Simulations are penalized with 150% surcharge.

Director personal liability: Directors who established or operated the shell entity are personally liable for uncovered taxes. If the arrangement constitutes fraudulent bankruptcy or criminal tax evasion, imprisonment of 1–5 years plus disqualification from managing companies for up to 5 years.
Cross-Border Withholding Tax Non-Compliance

Statutory sanction: Late-payment interest plus penalty under art. 20 LGT: the company must pay the omitted withholding amount. Penalty of 50% of the non-withheld amount; if fraudulent, 100%–150%. If treaty relief is rejected, the statutory rate applies (24% for royalties/interest to non-DTA).

Director personal liability: Directors who authorised the dividend distribution are jointly and severally liable for the unwithheld WHT. If the omitted WHT exceeds €120,000, criminal tax evasion charges may follow, with imprisonment up to 4 years and travel bans.
Failure to File Annual Accounts and Public Registry

Statutory sanction: Fines from €1,200 to €60,000 for late filing. Criminal false accounting (art. 290 Penal Code) carries 6 months–2 years imprisonment. AEAT may also penalize non-registration for IAE (Economic Activities Tax) from €300 to €2,000.

Director personal liability: Directors are personally liable for the corporate debts under art. 367 Capital Companies Act if annual accounts are not filed for two consecutive years. They may be disqualified from commercial activities for up to 5 years.
